title: Romania’s largest refinery suspends operations for technical overhaul
lead: Rompetrol announced that the largest refinery in Romania, Petromidia, is currently undergoing an overhaul, contradicting the minister of energy, Bogdan Ivan, who had stated that he had temporarily postponed it, according to Profit.ro . Minister Ivan also said he would restart Petrotel Lukoil refinery after he received an informal permit from the US’s OFAC and “reopened trading route” to bring crude oil into the country. "We have greatly increased crude oil imports, we have managed to temporarily postpone a technical overhaul of the Petromidia refinery, we are also working at full capacity at Petrobrazi, precisely to ensure that we have stability in Romania," minister Ivan recently declared.

title: Insurance Company VZP Warns Public of Fake Refund Emails
lead: Czech health insurance company VZP is warning the public about a surge of fraudulent emails promising refunds of insurance premiums. The scam, which has already tricked multiple victims, urges recipients to provide personal and banking details in exchange for sums around 11,580 crowns. Jan Svoboda, Director of VZP’s Security Department, said the scam emails are sophisticated and convincing. “We are registering an extreme wave of fraudulent emails bearing the VZP logo and a number of valid elements that can confuse recipients. The messages promise a refund of overpayment from health insurance, and dangerous emails could have arrived at up to hundreds of thousands of addresses,” he explained.

title: The Iran war and the cost of killing 'bad guys'
lead: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said Thursday that it "takes money to kill bad guys" when asked if the Pentagon had requested $200 billion in funding for the Iran war. But it could be substantial: The Pentagon's comptroller reportedly told lawmakers that the first six days of the war had cost $11.3 billion.

More than 7.1 million people passed through its doors, a 13% increase in visitors year on year and an all-time record for any UK museum or gallery.

title: Viktor Orbán refuses to agree to €90bn loan for Ukraine as EU leaders accuse him of betrayal
lead: German chancellor Friedrich Merz described Orbán’s U-turn on the loan Hungary had agreed to in December as ‘a gross act of disloyalty’ EU leaders fumed after Hungary’s prime minister, Viktor Orbán, refused to drop his opposition to a vital €90bn (£78bn) loan for Ukraine, accusing him of betrayal and acting in bad faith. German chancellor Friedrich Merz described Orbán’s U-turn on the loan Hungary had agreed to in December as “a gross act of disloyalty” adding: “I am firmly convinced that it will leave deep marks.”

title: Trump-appointed panel approves 24-karat gold coin featuring his face
lead: Federal law says living presidents can’t appear on currency, but commission approves design for US’s 250th birthday A federal arts commission on Thursday approved the final design for a 24-karat gold commemorative coin bearing Donald Trump ’s image to help celebrate the US’s 250th birthday on 4 July. title: Iran says Hormuz open to all but ‘enemy-linked’ ships amid US threat

French voters returned to the polls Sunday for the second and final round of municipal elections in over 1,500 communes. The race is expected to be extremely tight in Paris with Emmanuel Grégoire, heading a united left and green list, competing with conservative Rachida Dati and hard-left La France Insoumise candidate Sophia Chikirou. FRANCE 24's Antonia Kerrigan reports from Paris.

title: Italy’s justice referendum becomes key test for PM Meloni’s leadership
lead: Italy’s two-day referendum on whether or not to overhaul the country’s justice system has become a key test for Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni. If the “No” side wins, analysts say it will send a strong political signal and weaken her leadership. Accused by her opponents of threatening the judiciary's independence, the premier has doubled down on claims that if the reform does not go through, more “immigrants, rapists, pedophiles, drug dealers” will go free.
text:
Italy’s justice referendum becomes key test for PM Meloni’s leadership
Italy’s two-day referendum on whether or not to overhaul the country’s justice system has become a key test for Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni. If the “No” side wins, analysts say it will send a strong political signal and weaken her leadership. Accused by her opponents of threatening the judiciary's independence, the premier has doubled down on claims that if the reform does not go through, more “immigrants, rapists, pedophiles, drug dealers” will go free.
